policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.173: Implantable Intrathecal or Epidural Pain Pump
source_section: Policy/Criteria - Section I.A.1 Malignant Pain Trial
source_quote: Chronic intractable pain of malignant origin when all of the following criteria is met: a. Inadequate response to, or intolerable side effects from, noninvasive methods of pain control such as systemic opioids; b. Life expectancy > three months; c. No evidence of epidural metastatic lesion(s) or tumor encroachment of the thecal sac by imaging;
clinical_service_or_procedure: Preliminary trial of epidural or intrathecal opioid - Malignant Pain

criteria.description: Inadequate response or intolerable side effects from systemic opioids
No evidence of epidural metastasis or thecal sac encroachment on imaging

required_documentation: Oncology records documenting life expectancy > 3 months
Spine MRI/CT ruling out epidural metastases or cord compression
review_notes: Preliminary trial prerequisite for cancer-related intractable pain.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.173: Implantable Intrathecal or Epidural Pain Pump
source_section: Policy/Criteria - Section I.A.2 Non-Malignant Pain Trial
source_quote: Chronic intractable pain of nonmalignant origin (e.g. failed back surgery syndrome, complex regional pain syndrome) when all the following criteria are met: a. Pathology for the pain has been identified; b. Life expectancy is > three months; c. Failure or inability to tolerate other conservative treatment methods
clinical_service_or_procedure: Preliminary trial of epidural or intrathecal opioid - Non-Malignant Pain

criteria.description: Failure of conservative methods, psychological clearance, weaned opioids by ≥50%

required_documentation: Psychological evaluation ruling out major mental health cause
Opioid weaning records confirming ≥50% reduction prior to trial
review_notes: Requires 50% systemic opioid weaning and psychological evaluation.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.173: Implantable Intrathecal or Epidural Pain Pump
source_quote: None of the following contraindications: 1. Known allergies to materials in the implant; 2. Active alcohol or drug abuse, including but not limited to opioid addiction and intravenous drug abuse;

criteria.description: Active alcohol or drug abuse / untreated addiction
Diagnosis of dementia, psychosis, or active infection

review_notes: Contraindicated in active addiction, psychosis, or infection.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.173: Implantable Intrathecal or Epidural Pain Pump
source_quote: Chronic intractable pain of malignant origin when the above criteria for the preliminary trial are met, and all of the following: a. The trial provided ≥ 50% reduction in pain with minimal side effects;* b. Body size is sufficient to support the weight and bulk of the device;
clinical_service_or_procedure: Permanent implantable intrathecal pain pump - Malignant Pain (HCPCS E0782, E0783)

criteria.description: Trial provided ≥ 50% reduction in pain with minimal side effects
Body size sufficient to support weight and bulk of device

required_documentation: Surgical notes regarding device pocket feasibility
review_notes: Trial requirement may be reviewed by medical director for advanced terminal disease.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.173: Implantable Intrathecal or Epidural Pain Pump
source_quote: Severe chronic pain of non-malignant origin when the above criteria for the preliminary trial is met and all of the following: a. Preliminary trial provided ≥ 50% reduction in pain and increase in function with minimal side effects; b. There is a plan in place to continue to wean systemic opioids;
clinical_service_or_procedure: Permanent implantable intrathecal pain pump - Non-Malignant Pain (HCPCS E0782, E0783)

criteria.description: Trial provided ≥ 50% reduction in pain AND increase in function
Plan in place to continue to wean systemic opioids
No active coagulopathy, normal ICP, no anatomical spine barrier

required_documentation: Trial log confirming ≥50% pain relief and functional improvement
review_notes: Requires documented functional gain and ongoing opioid weaning protocol.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.173: Implantable Intrathecal or Epidural Pain Pump
source_quote: B. None of the following contraindications: 1. Known allergies to materials in the implant; 2. Active alcohol or drug abuse, including but not limited to opioid addiction and intravenous drug abuse; 3. Diagnosis of dementia or psychosis; 4. Active systemic infection; 5. Active infection at the site of implantation.

criteria.description: Active infection (systemic or at implant site)

review_notes: Absolute exclusion for infection, active abuse, dementia, or implant allergy.
